```{python}
import json
import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
from pathlib import Path
from IPython.display import display
rows = pd.read_csv('results/comparison.csv')
probes = pd.read_csv('results/source-precision-probes.csv')
diagnostics = json.loads(Path('results/diagnostics.json').read_text())
identity = json.loads(Path('results/run-identity.json').read_text())
counts = rows.outcome.value_counts()
probe_range = probes.groupby('point').native_pressure_bar.agg(['min','max'])
```

The literal source model gives `{python} str(counts.get('pass', 0))` passing,
`{python} str(counts.get('fail', 0))` failing and
`{python} str(counts.get('undetermined', 0))` undetermined nominal comparisons.
All `{python} str(len(rows))` nominal attempts and
`{python} str(len(probes))` source-precision probes are retained.
This is **numerical comparison against published model lines**, not comparison
with experimental symbols or physical validation.

The model uses Table 1's literal segment counts, diameters and dispersion
energies, the Table 3 binary interaction, one donor/one acceptor on each
component and zero association energies. Unlike-site edges also have zero
energy, so their association strength is zero under the source combining
rule. No familiar alternative CO2 diameter or fitted interaction is substituted.
The native declared bubble calculation solves pressure and vapor composition;
its zero incipient-vapor amount is intentional.

```{python}
display(rows)
display(probe_range)
display(probes)
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(7,4))
for T, r in rows.groupby('T_K'):
    ax.errorbar(r.x_sulfolane, r.reference_pressure_bar, yerr=r.tolerance_bar, fmt='o', label=f'{T:g} K source model')
    ax.scatter(r.x_sulfolane, r.native_pressure_bar, marker='x', label=f'{T:g} K native')
ax.set(xlabel='Liquid sulfolane mole fraction', ylabel='Bubble pressure / bar')
ax.legend()
fig.tight_layout()
plt.show()
display(pd.json_normalize(diagnostics))
```

The discrete points compare with the calibrated orange and green strokes of
Figure 1, printed p.6331, DOI `10.1021/acs.iecr.1c00176`. Error bars are the
fixed vertical raster allowance, **not experimental uncertainty**. Horizontal
readback uncertainty and printed-temperature rounding are tested separately
by the retained native probes. No line is interpolated between these sparse
points. The original raster, calibration, extraction configuration, pixel
coordinates and inspected overlay remain under `inputs/source/figure-1/`.

The nominal absolute errors span `{python} f'{rows.error_bar.min():.4g}'` to
`{python} f'{rows.error_bar.max():.4g}'` bar, compared with the fixed
`{python} str(rows.tolerance_bar.iloc[0])` bar allowance. The finite probe
ranges remain far above the source references; these declared precision probes
cannot explain the disagreement. Their extrema are not rigorous uncertainty
bounds and never enlarge the nominal allowance. Agreement of native pressure
and fugacity equations establishes numerical closure only. Density ordering
between phases of different composition is not imposed; distinct states,
positive normalized compositions and mechanical slopes remain visible.

The discrepancy belongs to the **literal declared source model comparison**.
The current evidence does not isolate a particular printed coefficient as its
cause, and no parameter correction is authorized. Exact fractional source
temperatures and a second independent extraction remain unavailable. Other
Figure 1 curves, Figures 2–10 and reactive MDEA comparisons remain uncompleted;
adjacent Kuranov total pressures cannot replace CO2 partial-pressure data.
